reason: Skipped for two reasons: only two fully sourced rows meet the 16-inch 16:10 2560x1600 120 Hz line (the layout needs four), and the Duex Float 2 Pro cannot be shown to place in the top three on brightness and weight. Blocked today (2026-11-26): storecheck.py returned HTTP 403 on every call (mobilepixels.us, uperfectmonitor.com, arzopa.com, sotsu.com); page fetches of mobilepixels.us, uperfect.com, uperfectmonitor.com and sotsu.com returned HTTP 429 on every retry, including a last retry after a 100-second wait; B&H and Adorama returned 403; amzcheck.py returned no output for either Amazon search. Angle F's report was cut off in my brief, so its rows and prices were not available to me. Rows: the Float 2 Pro and the ASUS ZenScreen MB16QHG are the only in-line screens with every cell sourced. I could not read the UPERFECT GR16DQ's brightness, weight, one-cable behaviour or stock notices, and I opened no SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2 page at all. The Arzopa Z1RC is fully measured but 60 Hz. Our Fold 16 QHD record carries no refresh rate. ASUS's US eshop shows the MB16QHG out of stock with 'Notify me' and no price (https://eshop.asus.com/us/90lm08ng-b011b0-asus-zenscreen-mb16qhg.html). Ranking: ASUS states 500 cd/m2 typical and 1.2 kg (2.65 lb) against the Float's 350 nits and 2.9 lb (Macworld). The desk leads put the UPERFECT at 400 nits and 1.7 lb for $189.99, and a search listing gives the SOTSU 400 nits; I verified none of the three. If those leads hold, the Float is fourth of four on makers' figures, which is the stated skip case. I did not bend the ranking or fill the UPERFECT and SOTSU cells from leads. Verified and ready for a rerun (angle A, with D's sourcing): Macworld's review (Simon Jary, Dec 16 2025, https://www.macworld.com/article/2961577/mobile-pixels-duex-float-2-pro-review-portable-screen.html) says the Float 2 Pro draws 7.5 W from the MacBook in a Limited Power Mode that caps brightness at 80%, needs a PD charger of 15 W or more for full brightness, and passes back up to 65 W. ASUS's product page says maximum brightness needs the adapter plugged in; Brandon Hill (PC Pro via TechRadar Pro, 28 March 2025) found 60% brightness on one USB-C cable and measured 417 cd/m2. ServeTheHome (Sam Sabinash, 23 May 2026) measured the Z1RC at 415.7 nits and 11.0 W at 100%, 60 Hz maximum. Apple (https://support.apple.com/en-us/126319): 254 ppi, up to 120 Hz, 99.6 Wh, 140 W adapter, MagSafe 3, three external displays on M5 Pro and four on M5 Max. Macworld's Mac roundup, re-read today, gives no monitor wattage, one-cable brightness cap, ppi, 140 W or MagSafe figure; the RTINGS page loaded without its picks. Parkablogs (Teoh Yi Chie, 20 June 2023) measured 238 nits against 400 advertised and 720 g on the UPERFECT UPlays C2, but I could not tie that model to the GR16DQ, which the store says was formerly the UGame C2. To finish: re-read the UPERFECT GR16DQ page (nits, weight, power note, stock), a SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2 maker or B&H page (specs, price) and the Mobile Pixels Fold 16 QHD refresh rate once the stores stop rate-limiting. If the UPERFECT's figures hold, the page should name it as the pick and give the Float the stacked-above-the-MacBook segment, or stay skipped if the Float falls outside the top three.
why_angle: Macworld's Mac roundup, the only cited rival page that lists the Float 2 Pro, gives no monitor wattage, one-cable brightness cap or 140 W comparison, and PCWorld's roundup (per the angle agents' reads) names none of these screens. The one-cable figures (Float 2 Pro 7.5 W with an 80% cap, ASUS 60% without its adapter, 65 W pass-back against Apple's 140 W) are what a 16-inch MacBook Pro owner needs, but they are sourced for only two in-line screens today.
